newsitem.title: USA: Salomon Bros U.S. March same store sales index up.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Bros U.S. March same store sales index up.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said its U.S. same-store sales growth index rose 4.4 percent in March, compared with a 5.4 percent rise a year ago.
This followed a 4.7 percent increase in February.
In a report, Salomon Brothers analysts said March sales were somewhat constrained by the timing of the Easter holiday, which resulted in the closing of stores on an important Sunday.

"Analytically, we believe that it is important to view March and April sales together due to the shift in the Easter holiday," Salomon analysts said. "Nonetheless, while there was some divergence by subsector in March, on balance, we believe that apparel retail results were somewhat weak while the discount store sector continued to show particular strength."

Salomon analysts also said that, despite recent strength in stock price for the retail group, strong inventory and expense control are expected to lead to retailers' earnings outpacing the earnings of the Standard & Poor's 500 beginning in the second or, at the latest, the third quarter of 1997.
